title: Altrincham mum warns of 'botched' £150 filler that cost £700 to fix

evidence_packet.title: Altrincham mum warns of 'botched' £150 filler that cost £700 to fix
evidence_packet.lead: Joanne Bauer says she stayed home for weeks after the cheap treatment affected her confidence
evidence_packet.summary: Joanne Bauer says she stayed home for weeks after the cheap treatment affected her confidence
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A mother-of-two said she refused to go out for weeks after "botched" under-eye fillers left her in searing pain - and has now urged others considering similar treatments to do careful research Joanne Bauer, 48, said she chose a £150 treatment she spotted on social media after being quoted about £495 elsewhere, and later had to spend more than £700 having it corrected "I wished I'd done some more homework" the finance director from Altrincham, Greater Manchester, said Her warning comes as a poll commissioned by the Professional Standards Authority for Health and Social Care found 46% of 1,000 UK adults surveyed believed all aesthetic practitioners were regulated by law The non-surgical aesthetics industry - including providers of Botox, dermal fillers, and chemical peels - is largely unregulated. In the UK, anyone can legally perform many non-surgical procedures without medical qualifications Last year the government promised to develop a licensing system for England, but it is yet to be introduced

title: Former Bolton footballer and family speak out about daughter's death

evidence_packet.title: Former Bolton footballer and family speak out about daughter's death
evidence_packet.lead: Dean Holden and his wife Danielle have spoken about their loss as they launch a new YouTube series
evidence_packet.summary: Dean Holden and his wife Danielle have spoken about their loss as they launch a new YouTube series
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A former Premier League footballer whose daughter died from meningococcal septicaemia have said they hope that by speaking out about their loss they can help others in the same situation Dean Holden and Danielle Nicholls lost their daughter Cici, aged 17 months, after she contracted meningococcal septicaemia , external while they were on holiday in Lanzarote in May 2012 Nicholls said it was important for the couple to talk openly about their "devastating" loss as they launch their new YouTube reality series charting their family life "warts and all" The mum-of-five told BBC Breakfast that her other four children "have saved my life" and "are my happiness and... my sunshine" She said the family used humour as a way to help them to cope with their loss and "I think that that's how you have to move forward", adding that "you have to see the brighter side (of life)" She said: "I didn't want the kids to think life was great and then our sister died, and life was horrible and it's so difficult because there is such sadness."

title: Greenfield homes were evacuated as fire raged at industrial site

evidence_packet.title: Greenfield homes were evacuated as fire raged at industrial site
evidence_packet.lead: An industrial unit near Oldham erupted in flames, with 45 homes evacuated
evidence_packet.summary: An industrial unit near Oldham erupted in flames, with 45 homes evacuated
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greenfield homes were evacuated as fire raged at industrial site - BBC News Image caption, Homes in two streets were evacuated as flames engulfed an industrial unit By Stewart Whittingham North West Published 16 August 2026 Families had to be evacuated from their homes in two streets after a huge fire broke out at a neighbouring industrial building. The blaze, which shot huge plumes of black and orange smoke into the sky, was spotted at just after 07:30 BST at a site off Wellington Road in Greenfield, near Oldham. Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service said 45 homes were evacuated in Wellington Road and Knoll Close, which backs on to the burning building. Residents have now returned to their homes, with fire crews using gas detectors to ensure it was safe to do so, a spokesperson said. Image caption, The site backs on to houses on Knoll Close More than 10 fire engines along with a number of aerial ladder units and specialist appliances from across Greater Manchester were sent to the scene of the blaze. "Our crews remain at the scene, continuing their work alongside partners to make the site safe," the fire service added. A cordon was put in place during the incident and nearby roads were shut while crews tackled the fire. People were asked to avoid the area. evidence_packet.title: Ex-Stockport player bounces back from cancer to set up Dubai club

evidence_packet.summary: Bader Al-Akkad's "long journey" took in the war in Syria and a career-ending cancer diagnosis
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A former footballer whose playing career was cut short by cancer has said co-founding a club in Dubai aimed at "giving people second chances" felt like "a massive achievement" Bader Al-Akkad, from Manchester, had to leave Stockport County's academy side after being diagnosed with Hodgkin lymphoma in 2021, ending his dreams of a professional contract After being given the all-clear, he started Phoenix United with his brother Amer, 27, to provide both sporting and academic opportunities to those wanting to follow their own footballing dreams "It's been a long journey of building... and to take this step now has been a massive achievement for us," said Bader, who is preparing for the side's first season in the UAE Third Division Bader and Amer were born in Manchester to Syrian parents, but spent their early years in Damascus after his family returned there They left Syria for the UK in 2012, a year after anti-government protests and a violent crackdown had escalated into conflict

title: The Stockport milkman who became a hero during audacious WW2 raid

evidence_packet.title: The Stockport milkman who became a hero during audacious WW2 raid
evidence_packet.lead: James Conway was among 12 men chosen to be part of a secret mission known as Operation Frankton
evidence_packet.summary: James Conway was among 12 men chosen to be part of a secret mission known as Operation Frankton
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Sixteen-year-old James Conway was working as a milkman when World War Two broke out in the September of 1939 Conway, from Edgeley in Stockport, signed up to join the Royal Marines where he trained for a secret mission, later named Operation Frankton He was among 12 men chosen to be part of what was widely considered to be one of the most audacious raids during the war Conway's story has featured in BBC Radio Manchester's Hidden Manchester series, which shares the forgotten, untold and heroic stories of the region By March 1942, Britain was struggling to fight back against Nazi Germany The mission was to attack enemy German ships, known as blockade runners, moored at the port of Bordeaux in occupied France

title: Heatwave blaze spree was 'busiest in Greater Manchester fire boss's 26-year career'

evidence_packet.title: Heatwave blaze spree was 'busiest in Greater Manchester fire boss's 26-year career'
evidence_packet.lead: Assistant chief fire officer Jim Willmott said he had never seen the control room so hectic
evidence_packet.summary: Assistant chief fire officer Jim Willmott said he had never seen the control room so hectic
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fire chiefs in Greater Manchester have said the service is experiencing its busiest period in decades - as a series of serious blazes broke out at the peak of the recent UK heatwave Crews were already dealing with a large wildfire near Oldham on Wednesday when a semi-detached house also went up in flames in south Manchester the next day A raft of fires across the country, including devastating blazes in the West Midlands, later prompted the government to issue a temporary ban on disposable barbecues Greater Manchester's Chief Fire Officer Dave Russel thanked crews for their work in an "exceptionally busy period" while his deputy Jim Willmott said firefighters had received 1,200 calls on Thursday Willmott told BBC Radio Manchester : "Yesterday I was in the fire control room for North West Fire Control - it really was the most incredibly busy period I have ever seen in my 26 years of service." Earlier in the month crews stood down from wildfires on two stretches of moorland near Dove Stone Reservoir and at Tintwistle and Swineshore

title: Greater Manchester Police arrest alleged driver in 100mph stolen Amazon van pursuit

evidence_packet.title: Greater Manchester Police arrest alleged driver in 100mph stolen Amazon van pursuit
evidence_packet.lead: A suspected thief is held after leading police on a 40-minute chase in a stolen Amazon van
evidence_packet.summary: A suspected thief is held after leading police on a 40-minute chase in a stolen Amazon van
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A suspected thief was arrested after leading traffic police on a 100mph chase in a stolen Amazon delivery van carrying £1,000 worth of parcels The 25-year-old was held after officers pursued the van from Wigan, in Greater Manchester, through Bolton and into Chorley in Lancashire, where the van crashed into pedestrian barriers and a vehicle stopped at traffic lights Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said over the course of 40 minutes, the van had been driven three times over the speed limit, reaching around 100mph, injured a cyclist and caused significant damage to multiple pieces of street furniture No serious injuries were reported. The arrested man has been bailed pending further inquiries GMP received a 999 call at around 18:23 BST on Wednesday to report the van had been stolen Officers located the vehicle within 15 minutes and began to follow it. They tried to stop it without a pursuit, but the driver sped away

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A former Premier League footballer whose daughter died from meningococcal septicaemia have said they hope that by speaking out about their loss they can help others in the same situation Dean Holden and Danielle Nicholls lost their daughter Cici, aged 17 months, after she contracted meningococcal septicaemia , external while they were on holiday in Lanzarote in May 2012 Nicholls said it was important for the couple to talk openly about their "devastating" loss as they launch their new YouTube reality series charting their family life "warts and all" The mum-of-five told BBC Breakfast that her other four children "have saved my life" and "are my happiness and... my sunshine" She said the family used humour as a way to help them to cope with their loss and "I think that that's how you have to move forward", adding that "you have to see the brighter side (of life)" She said: "I didn't want the kids to think life was great and then our sister died, and life was horrible and it's so difficult because there is such sadness."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A former footballer whose playing career was cut short by cancer has said co-founding a club in Dubai aimed at "giving people second chances" felt like "a massive achievement" Bader Al-Akkad, from Manchester, had to leave Stockport County's academy side after being diagnosed with Hodgkin lymphoma in 2021, ending his dreams of a professional contract After being given the all-clear, he started Phoenix United with his brother Amer, 27, to provide both sporting and academic opportunities to those wanting to follow their own footballing dreams "It's been a long journey of building... and to take this step now has been a massive achievement for us," said Bader, who is preparing for the side's first season in the UAE Third Division Bader and Amer were born in Manchester to Syrian parents, but spent their early years in Damascus after his family returned there They left Syria for the UK in 2012, a year after anti-government protests and a violent crackdown had escalated into conflict

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Sixteen-year-old James Conway was working as a milkman when World War Two broke out in the September of 1939 Conway, from Edgeley in Stockport, signed up to join the Royal Marines where he trained for a secret mission, later named Operation Frankton He was among 12 men chosen to be part of what was widely considered to be one of the most audacious raids during the war Conway's story has featured in BBC Radio Manchester's Hidden Manchester series, which shares the forgotten, untold and heroic stories of the region By March 1942, Britain was struggling to fight back against Nazi Germany The mission was to attack enemy German ships, known as blockade runners, moored at the port of Bordeaux in occupied France

title: Greater Manchester Police arrest alleged driver in 100mph stolen Amazon van pursuit

evidence_packet.title: Greater Manchester Police arrest alleged driver in 100mph stolen Amazon van pursuit
evidence_packet.lead: A suspected thief was arrested after leading traffic police on a 100mph chase in a stolen Amazon delivery van carrying £1,000 worth of parcels The 25-year-old was held after officers pursued the van from Wigan, in Greater Manchester, through Bolton and into Chorley in Lancashire
evidence_packet.summary: A suspected thief was arrested after leading traffic police on a 100mph chase in a stolen Amazon delivery van carrying £1,000 worth of parcels The 25-year-old was held after officers pursued the van from Wigan, in Greater Manchester, through Bolton and into Chorley in Lancashire
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A suspected thief was arrested after leading traffic police on a 100mph chase in a stolen Amazon delivery van carrying £1,000 worth of parcels The 25-year-old was held after officers pursued the van from Wigan, in Greater Manchester, through Bolton and into Chorley in Lancashire, where the van crashed into pedestrian barriers and a vehicle stopped at traffic lights Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said over the course of 40 minutes, the van had been driven three times over the speed limit, reaching around 100mph, injured a cyclist and caused significant damage to multiple pieces of street furniture No serious injuries were reported. The arrested man has been bailed pending further inquiries GMP received a 999 call at around 18:23 BST on Wednesday to report the van had been stolen Officers located the vehicle within 15 minutes and began to follow it. They tried to stop it without a pursuit, but the driver sped away

News Charlotte Hall Local De
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Salford family say police are failing them over 'relentless' hate attacks on their home Masked teens throwing rocks and hurling abuse have left a Syrian-Kurdish couple wanting to leave the area, despite working in local NHS services for years. News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 17:48, 16 Aug 2026 A family in Salford feel they are being ‘forced out’ of their home due to relentless abuse from a group of local teens - including eggs and rocks being thrown at their house The attacks have been going on regularly for almost two years and often feature racist or islamophobic abuse, leading the family to believe the harassment is targeted “I don’t want to leave my home, it’s an amazing area,” said Aram, 35, whose name has been changed for peace of mind, “But I feel I’m being forced out by these people who just have no shame. It keeps happening again and again and again. That’s why I’m upset.” Aram and his wife, who are both Kurdish, fled from Syria more than a decade ago and work as a pharmacist and doctor in the Salford area. They originally lived in Fallowfield in Manchester, before they became eligible for a council house in a scheme through Salford Hospital for hi View 3 Images Egg thrown at the family's home

Maybe it’s the devil we don’t know that we need to go with.” View 6 Images Oldham is known for its divisive politics but News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 06:41, 16 Aug 2026 Some in Oldham are ready to welcome ‘the devil they don’t know’ after a months-long ‘Mexican stand off’ keeps going around in ‘vicious circles’ At the end of July, Oldham Council officially declared it is breaking the law with the cause of this being an ongoing row over who should be leading the local authority. After three months with no one in charge, things are still in limbo with officers continuing to use emergency Last month, the council’s top legal boss Alex Bougatef declared the council was acting unlawfully without anyone in charge issuing what is called a Section 5 Repor t. This sets in motion a process that could see outside intervention if no solution is found at a meeting on August Commissioners are officials sent by the UK Government to help run councils deemed to be failing or breaking the law with little local say. Often brought in when a council goes effectively bankrupt, commissioners being imposed due to an unshifting political quarrel like Oldham's i Some parties think this scenario is unlikely given voters will be going to the polls again next May to elect another third of councillors potentially changing the council's makeup. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Real Life 'I got the s**t kicked out of me - but it made me realise who I needed to help' Advisor to some of the UK and US' top politicians, 32-year-old Pablo O'Hana from Withington left school with few qualifications and never went to university View Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 06:34, 16 Aug 2026 Updated 13:02, 16 Aug 2026 Walking into Westminster's Strangers' Bar on his third day in Parliament, Pablo O'Hana came up against the stuffy elitism of British politics. Aged 19 and a brand-new staffer for Manchester The question took Pablo aback; not only did it come barely seconds after their introduction, but its meaning wasn't immediately obvious. He soon realised the MP was referring to which university he attended: "Oxford or Cambridge?" The surreal moment made him realise just how at odds his own upbringing in Withington was compared to the MPs and staffers he would now rub shoulders with at the bar. Especially when taking into account that he had never attended university, not helped by his 'hellish' school yea "I was actually all right in primary school," Pablo said. "Secondary school was where everything went off the rails "I mean, it's easy now to look back and think, 'Well, you know, I did ballet, I had a passion for animal rights, I was obsessed with Titanic.' Now I look back and think, well, no wonder I had the s**t kicked out of me!"

title: The truth about Piccadilly Gardens

evidence_packet.title: The truth about Piccadilly Gardens
evidence_packet.lead: Piccadilly Gardens The truth about Piccadilly Gardens SPECIAL REPORT: Behind the "Crackadilly" headlines and social media outrage lies a very different story about Manchester's busiest public space.
evidence_packet.summary: Piccadilly Gardens The truth about Piccadilly Gardens SPECIAL REPORT: Behind the "Crackadilly" headlines and social media outrage lies a very different story about Manchester's busiest public space. Stephen Topping reports
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Piccadilly Gardens The truth about Piccadilly Gardens SPECIAL REPORT: Behind the "Crackadilly" headlines and social media outrage lies a very different story about Manchester's busiest public space. Stephen Topping reports. View 21 Images There are di News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 06:29, 16 Aug 2026 Look up Piccadilly Gardens on the internet and you would be forgiven for staying away from the place. No other corner of Manchester is as fiercely debated, meticulously scrutinised or bitterly maligned in 2026 And with the political gaze fixating on the city in recent months, that discussion has been ramped up. Piccadilly Gardens is the most high-profile public space in the same city centre that now hosts Number 10 North , while the new Prime Minister is the same man who served as Grea It is in this context which Piccadilly Gardens is now being debated, fairly or otherwise. What was previously a hot talking point for Mancunians is now a hefty stick for commentators to hammer Andy Burnham with Manchester council accepts Piccadilly Gardens is not 'good enough at the moment'. Viral social media videos which capture moments of violence and alleged drug use are impossible to ignore, while the Manchester Evening News has reported on police activity in Piccadilly Gardens eve But those flashpoints don't tell the whole story. More than 40,000 people pass through Piccadilly Gardens every day, and hundreds make it a destination in itself. Views among people who visit the area are more varied and nuanced than those found in social media comment sections

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Police name suspect after 48-hour roof stand off in Salford A man has been charged with a string of offences following the incident on Ash Street over the weekend News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 08:01, 17 Aug 2026 View Image A man has been charged after police were involved in a 48-hour roof stand off in Salford The incident started on Ash Street on Thursday evening (August 13) when police, firefighters and paramedics were called over reports of a man on a roof. A cordon was put in place in the area and specialist police were involved in a stand-off with the man throughout Friday and Sat The man was eventually pulled from the roof and arrested on Saturday afternoon. Simon Harris, 37, of no fixed abode, has now been charged following the incident He has been charged with eight offences in total. The charges are: four counts of criminal damage, two counts of assault of an emergency worker, intentionally/recklessly causing a public nuisance and burglary dwelling and theft Mr Harris has been remanded into custody. He is due to appear at Manchester and Salford Magistrates' Court today (August 17)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Salford family say police are failing them over 'relentless' hate attacks on their home Masked teens throwing rocks and hurling abuse have left a Syrian-Kurdish couple wanting to leave the area, despite working in local NHS services for years. News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 17:48, 16 Aug 2026 A family in Salford feel they are being ‘forced out’ of their home due to relentless abuse from a group of local teens - including eggs and rocks being thrown at their house The attacks have been going on regularly for almost two years and often feature racist or islamophobic abuse, leading the family to believe the harassment is targeted “I don’t want to leave my home, it’s an amazing area,” said Aram, 35, whose name has been changed for peace of mind, “But I feel I’m being forced out by these people who just have no shame. It keeps happening again and again and again. That’s why I’m upset.” Aram and his wife, who are both Kurdish, fled from Syria more than a decade ago and work as a pharmacist and doctor in the Salford area. They originally lived in Fallowfield in Manchester, before they became eligible for a council house in a scheme through Salford Hospital for hi View 3 Images Egg thrown at the family's home

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton 'Don't go up there': Weird moorland sacrifices, strange legends, and the fight to rebuild 'Two Lads' A mysterious presence on the West Pennine moors for centuries, the stone monuments, once believed to be the location of Druid sacrifices, are b News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 17:30, 16 Aug 2026 Hundreds of people joined an archaeological dig days before stone cairns which date back to the Bronze age are rebuilt The ‘Two Lads’ stone monuments which have stood on the moors for time immemorial on Crooked Edge Hill, an outlying summit on Winter Hill, were dismantled in July and are now in the process of being rebuilt The iconic moorland stone landmarks high up on the West Pennine moors, north of Bolton , are on the Smithills estate managed by the Woodland Trust After a public consultation the trust is rebuilding the cairns into beehive shapes, with a new dry stone wall surrounding them It is hoped the restored monuments will continue to be a popular destination, with views of Bolton, the Manchester and Salford skyline, Liverpool docks, North Wales and even Barrow all being visible from the peak

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Real Life 'I got the s**t kicked out of me - but it made me realise who I needed to help' Advisor to some of the UK and US' top politicians, 32-year-old Pablo O'Hana from Withington left school with few qualifications and never went to university View Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 06:34, 16 Aug 2026 Updated 13:02, 16 Aug 2026 Walking into Westminster's Strangers' Bar on his third day in Parliament, Pablo O'Hana came up against the stuffy elitism of British politics. Aged 19 and a brand-new staffer for Manchester The question took Pablo aback; not only did it come barely seconds after their introduction, but its meaning wasn't immediately obvious. He soon realised the MP was referring to which university he attended: "Oxford or Cambridge?" The surreal moment made him realise just how at odds his own upbringing in Withington was compared to the MPs and staffers he would now rub shoulders with at the bar. Especially when taking into account that he had never attended university, not helped by his 'hellish' school yea "I was actually all right in primary school," Pablo said. "Secondary school was where everything went off the rails "I mean, it's easy now to look back and think, 'Well, you know, I did ballet, I had a passion for animal rights, I was obsessed with Titanic.' Now I look back and think, well, no wonder I had the s**t kicked out of me!"

After three months with no one in charge, things are still in limbo with officers continuing to use emergency Last month, the council’s top legal boss Alex Bougatef declared the council was acting unlawfully without anyone in charge issuing what is called a Section 5 Repor t. This sets in motion a process that could see outside intervention if no solution is found at a meeting on August Commissioners are officials sent by the UK Government to help run councils deemed to be failing or breaking the law with little local say. Often brought in when a council goes effectively bankrupt, commissioners being imposed due to an unshifting political quarrel like Oldham's i Some parties think this scenario is unlikely given voters will be going to the polls again next May to elect another third of councillors potentially changing the council's makeup. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Piccadilly Gardens The truth about Piccadilly Gardens SPECIAL REPORT: Behind the "Crackadilly" headlines and social media outrage lies a very different story about Manchester's busiest public space. Stephen Topping reports. View 21 Images There are di News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 06:29, 16 Aug 2026 Look up Piccadilly Gardens on the internet and you would be forgiven for staying away from the place. Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Friday 10 July 2026 at 6:00pm Anthony McGrath accused Andy Burnham of protecting peodophiles. A bomb hoaxer claimed he would target a town hall after accusing Andy Burnham of “protecting paedophiles" and threatening MPs, a court has heard Anthony McGrath, 57, claimed the bombs would arrive from Russia and added: “Stop protecting #paedophiles @AndyBurnhamGM because the town hall will also be removed.” Posting on X in November 2025, McGrath also threatened Greater Manchester Police headquarters unless they returned property belonging to him, Liverpool Crown Court heard on Friday 10 July In January and February 2024 he sent a series of threatening emails to professionals, including Salford MP Rebecca Long-Bailey and Sir Robert Buckland, who at the time was MP for South Swindon, as well as a judge, solicitor, chartered surveyor and Nat West bank strategist McGrath, of Sale, Greater Manchester, was given a community order after the court heard he was suffering with his mental health at the time and had been sectioned following his arrest Martyn Walsh, prosecuting, said in one email sent to Ms Long-Bailey, McGrath said: “You all messed with the wrong person. My army is much bigger considering I have Russian and Chinese support. We will be armed and shoot to kill.”

Credit: Google Maps A murder investigation has been launched after a 40-year-old man died in hospital weeks after being stabbed in a "shocking" attack
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Friday 10 July 2026 at 8:00am Steven Dossett was treated for stab wounds at the scene and rushed to hospital but died days later. Credit: Google Maps A murder investigation has been launched after a 40-year-old man died in hospital weeks after being stabbed in a "shocking" attack Emergency services were called to Hale Lane in Failsworth at around 9:50pm on Friday, 19 June, following reports of an altercation Steven Dossett was treated for stab wounds at the scene and rushed to hospital. Greater Manchester Police have confirmed that he died from his injuries on Saturday, 4 July Detectives say they are continuing to pursue multiple lines of enquiry Five people - four men and one woman aged between 17 and 45 - were initially arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm and assault offences. They have since been released on bail while investigations continue Detective Chief Inspector Anna Barker, the Senior Investigating Officer, said: "This was a shocking attack, which has now evolved into a murder investigation following the death of Steven last week."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Crews were already dealing with a large wildfire near Oldham on Wednesday when a semi-detached house also went up in flames in south Manchester the next day A raft of fires across the country, including devastating blazes in the West Midlands, later prompted the government to issue a temporary ban on disposable barbecues Greater Manchester's Chief Fire Officer Dave Russel thanked crews for their work in an "exceptionally busy period" while his deputy Jim Willmott said firefighters had received 1,200 calls on Thursday Willmott told BBC Radio Manchester : "Yesterday I was in the fire control room for North West Fire Control - it really was the most incredibly busy period I have ever seen in my 26 years of service." title: Greater Manchester Police arrest alleged driver in 100mph stolen Amazon van pursuit

evidence_packet.title: Greater Manchester Police arrest alleged driver in 100mph stolen Amazon van pursuit
evidence_packet.lead: The 25-year-old was held after officers pursued the van from Wigan, in Greater Manchester, through Bolton and into Chorley in Lancashire, where the van crashed into pedestrian barriers and a vehicle stopped at traffic lights Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said over the course of
evidence_packet.summary: The 25-year-old was held after officers pursued the van from Wigan, in Greater Manchester, through Bolton and into Chorley in Lancashire, where the van crashed into pedestrian barriers and a vehicle stopped at traffic lights Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said over the course of
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The 25-year-old was held after officers pursued the van from Wigan, in Greater Manchester, through Bolton and into Chorley in Lancashire, where the van crashed into pedestrian barriers and a vehicle stopped at traffic lights Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said over the course of 40 minutes, the van had been driven three times over the speed limit, reaching around 100mph, injured a cyclist and caused significant damage to multiple pieces of street furniture No serious injuries were reported. The arrested man has been bailed pending further inquiries GMP received a 999 call at around 18:23 BST on Wednesday to report the van had been stolen Officers located the vehicle within 15 minutes and began to follow it. They tried to stop it without a pursuit, but the driver sped away The suspect was arrested at the scene of the crash on suspicion of theft of a motor vehicle, dangerous driving, failure to stop, driving under the influence of a controlled substance and possession of Class A and C drugs

Another 6,232 were accessing short-term care through services such as Strengths highlighted in the CQC report include timely assessments for most people, with the starting point of all assessments being what is important to the individual and what they want to achieve. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Council is reminding residents to recycle electrical items responsibly this summer due to dangers posed to waste collection crews As temperatures rise and the use of electrical items such as fans, portable chargers, and other rechargeable items increase, the council is urging residents to ensure unwanted electricals are taken to the correct recycling facilities Research from Material Focus has highlighted the growing popularity of low-cost electrical products, often known as ‘FastTech’, which can be easily forgotten, thrown away, or incorrectly disposed of. Many of these items contain batteries and valuable materials that can be recover When electrical items are placed in black and brown bins, they can also become damaged during collection and processing. This can cause batteries to spark, leading to fires that put waste and recycling crews at risk and can cause significant damage to vehicles and facilities Councillor Paul Kenny, portfolio holder for planning, environmental services and transport, said: "We know that during periods of hot weather, fans are often essential items to help people cool down, but when these products reach the end of their life, they should never be thrown "Electrical items and batteries can cause fires if damaged, putting our collection crews and staff at risk. By taking unwanted electricals to the correct recycling point, residents can help protect our workers, reduce waste, and ensure valuable materials are recovered and reused

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

Hidden in plain sight in Chinatown, it’s the kind of place chefs recommend, food writers praise, and regulars quietly keep going back to Jay Rayner called it “everything it should be” when he visited in 2021, which is about right. It’s intimate, informal, very good value and usually busy enough to make you feel smug if you’ve managed to get a table without waiting The pho is obviously a very good choice. So are the bánh mì. So is most of the menu, to be honest. But for the next Open Fire Dining Club , Pho Cue are stepping out of Chinatown and heading to Torr Vale Mill for something a little different They’ll be joining Tartuffe on 22 and 23 August for a menu that looks at Vietnamese cooking through a few different routes: the French influence that still runs through parts of the cuisine, the traditional use of fire found across Vietnam, and Cue’s more modern approach to Vietn There’s a continuation from the Porta dinner here too. Ben Armstrong, chief executive of Cytix, said: “We chose Northern Gritstone for their conviction in investing in deeptech companies in the North of England with global ambition. “Northern Gritstone and Cytix share the belief that software change is becoming a key risk for organisations and those that build software need a solution that scales with the current pace of development. “We’re also grateful to the existing investors that have backed us since the early days and increased their commitment because they've seen the thesis play out.” Ben added: “Software is changing. “AI-assisted development means change now happens at machine speed. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Events Networking South - Stockport - September Networking South - Stockport - September Official Chamber Post FREE or £22.00 for non-members Edgeley Park, Stockport County FC, Hardcastle Road, Stockport, SK3 9DD Tuesday 8 Sep 8:30am - 10:30am Sponsored By Forbes Solicitors Book This instalment is kindly sponsored by Forbes Solicitors who are a series sponsor this year, and are making their way across Greater Manchester to keep the region updated The format will include networking, followed by a brief welcome and updates from the Chamber, sponsor and partner. There will then be a 60-second round and more networking Refreshments (pastries and fruit along with tea/coffee) will be provided We are open, inclusive and welcoming, and we celebrate the diversity which makes up our city region.
